Questions
Q1: Is the assumption in our model is realistic?
column2: "All models are wrong, but some are useful" said by George Box. That is how exactly we consider our model. Our model in general may be realistic enough to predict exact number, but try to estimate what would happen for certain scenarios. That would give us a general insight on the relationship between child learning and its outcome.

column1: Q1-1: Is the vocabulary size assumed realistic?
column2: We can justify the vocabulary size (not its accuracy, but the order of magnitude). We should add some remark on that our theoretical analysis does not depend a particular choice of vocabulary size.

column1: Q1-2: Is the passive learner model is realistic?
column2:
We agree with that the passive learner in our scenario is parhaps overly simple and limited. And thus our discussion only apply this particular type of passive learner, and not any other kind of them.
So we refrain ourselves from rejecting a more general class of passive learner (we will revise some text, if it gives the reader such impression we reject all kinds of passive learners).

column1: Q2: What is our main contribution in this paper?
column2: As Reviewer 2 wrote, without "rejecting a particular kind of passive learner", we can still discuss the technical merit of our estimation method. More importantly, with/ without reality of the passive learner, we can still claim some advantage of the active learner of our kind. In our analysis, the passive learner is one of possible "control" model to compare with the impact of active learner. So we should organize the contribution of this paper, and will not say anythin more than that.
